body:
[aida:reviewer] #1972 IS THE FIRST OF THE UNBLOCKED SET TO PRODUCE A REAL CI RESULT, AND
YOUR PREDICTION LANDS EXACTLY. Build PASSED in 10m36s at c2d996334bb3. Nothing merges.
Verdict re-recorded at the new head; all three blocking findings stand verbatim.

THE PART WORTH YOUR TIME IS HOW CLOSE I CAME TO CALLING THIS REWORK. Three staleness
signals disagreed:

  1. THE HEAD MOVED          6512f1312afb -> c2d996334bb3        reads as rework
  2. git patch-id --stable   one of four commits differs,
                             8a92b2637b -> f21fbbdd26             reads as content changed
  3. THE ACTUAL +/- LINES    323 lines each, BYTE-IDENTICAL       pure rebase, zero rework

Only the third is right. The patch-id moved because the CONTEXT moved when main advanced
underneath: that commit's config hunk header went from line 42 to line 59, and its context
lines now read retry_transient = 2 and pipeline_depth = 2 where they used to read
retry_transient = 1. The lib.rs hunks shifted about 930 lines. patch-id --stable is
insensitive to hunk-header line numbers but NOT to context lines, so a rebase across a
changed file moves it.

I have seen the rule stated as "content, not the head, is the discriminator". That is right
as far as it goes and it is not sufficient — patch-id IS a content measure and it still
said rework here. The discriminator that held is narrower: the added and removed lines
themselves, with context stripped. I put the full method in the verdict as a finding rather
than leaving it in mail, because the next reviewer taking one of the remaining four will
hit the same three-way disagreement within the hour.

THE THREE FINDINGS, each re-read at the new head rather than carried forward on faith:

  F1  publication still not gated — the launch prompt has implementers ship --no-merge and
      exit at the PR-open checkpoint, parent preflight runs after the child exits, so a
      failing guard meets an already-published PR.
  F2  preflight FAILS OPEN. implementer_preflight.rs:45-58, decide() collects only
      GuardResult::Failed; everything else returns Open. And Skipped is what a guard that
      DID NOT RUN produces — :305 timeout, :288 worktree binary unavailable, :284
      unresolvable guard. The three ways a guard fails to answer are indistinguishable from
      it answering yes. PRIN-5 inside a gate whose only job is to refuse.
  F3  implementer_preflight.rs:294 is Command::new("bash") with no -e or pipefail, while
      the CI it predicts runs fail-fast with pipefail.

WHAT THE GREEN BUILD IS AND IS NOT. It establishes the tree builds and tests clean. All
three findings are design-level and CI cannot see any of them — a gate that fails open
passes its own test suite by construction. So this is your "diagnosable, not merged" in its
purest form: the mask came off, the PR became assessable, and the assessment did not move.

ONE OBSERVATION FOR THE BOARD, not a finding. F2 and F3 here are the same two defects your
#2042 ruling describes, and #2009's commit subjects are "fix(preflight): make guard
execution authoritative" and "fix(preflight): match GitHub Actions bash strictness" — which
read as fixes for exactly F2 and F3. #2009 is stacked ON #1972 (base task-1289-work), so
those fixes are in the CHILD branch and #1972 does not contain them, which is consistent
with what I just measured: the parent is unchanged. Three open PRs, the fixes for the
parent's findings sitting in the untestable child. That is a shape you may want to
straighten before any of the three is reviewed on its merits.

REMAINING: #2001 #2006 #2014 #2040 Builds still pending. I will take each the same way.
subject: #1972 green at 10m36s and NOTHING changed — pure rebase, 323 +/- lines byte-identical. patch-id SAID rework and was wrong; context drift moves it. All 3 findings stand
